card.title: That One Look
card.instruction: Choose one small look, phrase, silence, or gesture and treat it as the clearest evidence of what everything truly means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You texted 'thanks.' for covering your shift. Are we just colleagues now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was rushing. You're my best man. Help me choose ties.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Plain black. That full stop makes this a formal appointment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your speech is after dinner. Tell the story about our disastrous holiday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll list the dates and expenses. That full stop says we're past finding it funny.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats the thanks full stop as relationship evidence, A3 uses it to select formal ties, and A5 uses it to strip humor from a shared holiday speech.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's best-man role and tie request cause A3's formal black choice; B4's holiday-story request causes A5's date-and-expense version.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects the rushed text interpretation and gives A meaningful wedding responsibilities.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's affectionate shared story but filters its delivery through the original punctuation.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies a shift-cover text and B2 establishes the friendship and best-man role.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's dates-and-expenses choice grows from B4's holiday story and A's formal reading.

coach2.missing: No essential gap about the holiday is needed to understand the chosen dry treatment.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; one precise cue continues to determine practical choices despite contrary evidence.
